```{python}
#| label: load-summaries
# Small committed summaries written by pipeline/build_cohorts.py, plus the design
# targets from config.yaml. Every number in the prose below is one of these
# variables; nothing is typed by hand.
import json
import pandas as pd
import yaml
pop      = json.load(open("results/population_summary.json"))
manifest = json.load(open("results/release_manifest.json"))
cfg      = yaml.safe_load(open("config.yaml"))

def n(x):
    return f"{int(x):,}"

fl_pool             = n(pop["fl_pool_last_seen"])       # every simulant ever recorded in Florida, once
fl_finder_pool      = n(pop["fl_residents_finder_year"])
finder_year         = pop["finder_year"]
fl_simulants        = n(pop["fl_simulants"])            # 2020 census residents, for the official-count check
registry_rows       = n(manifest["files"]["registry.csv"]["rows"])
finder_500k_rows    = n(manifest["files"]["finder_500k.csv"]["rows"])
finder_100k_rows    = n(manifest["files"]["finder_100k.csv"]["rows"])
overlap_500k_target = n(cfg["cohorts"]["overlap_500k_target"])
overlap_100k_target = n(cfg["cohorts"]["overlap_100k_target"])

# The Key Features quote the design targets as facts about the files, which is
# only honest while the build hits them exactly; fail the render otherwise.
for k in ("500k", "100k"):
    assert manifest["overlaps"][f"finder_{k}"]["overlap_simulants"] == cfg["cohorts"][f"overlap_{k}_target"]
assert manifest["overlaps"]["finder_finder_simulants"] == cfg["cohorts"]["overlap_finder_finder_target"]

# --- everything else the prose quotes, named as in OUTLINE.md's computed-values table ---
err   = json.load(open("results/error_rates.json"))["realised"]
lb    = json.load(open("results/linkage_baseline.json"))
pairs = json.load(open("results/pair_agreement.json"))["finder_500k.csv"]
qa    = json.load(open("results/age_sex_qa.json"))["registry.csv"]
env   = json.load(open("results/environment.json"))
fcds  = pd.read_csv(cfg["paths"]["age_sex_target"], comment="#")

def pct(x, d=1):
    return f"{100 * x:.{d}f}%"

files, ov = manifest["files"], manifest["overlaps"]
registry_simulants     = n(files["registry.csv"]["distinct_simulants"])
registry_dupe_rows     = manifest["registry_duplicate_rows"]
finder_500k_simulants  = n(files["finder_500k.csv"]["distinct_simulants"])
finder_100k_simulants  = n(files["finder_100k.csv"]["distinct_simulants"])
overlap_500k_simulants = n(ov["finder_500k"]["overlap_simulants"])
overlap_100k_simulants = n(ov["finder_100k"]["overlap_simulants"])
overlap_500k_pairs     = n(ov["finder_500k"]["true_pairs"])
overlap_100k_pairs     = n(ov["finder_100k"]["true_pairs"])
overlap_finder_finder  = ov["finder_finder_simulants"]
match_prevalence_500k  = round(ov["finder_500k"]["match_prevalence"], 3)
match_prevalence_100k  = round(ov["finder_100k"]["match_prevalence"], 3)
fl_share_census        = pct(pop["fl_share_census"])
pop_ssn_never          = pct(pop["pop_ssn_never"], 2)
registry_ssn_missing   = pct(err["registry.csv"]["ssn_missing"], 2)
finder_ssn_missing     = pct(err["finder_500k.csv"]["ssn_missing"])
err_ssn_transposed     = n(err["finder_500k.csv"]["ssn_transposed"])
size_registry_mb, size_finder500k_mb, size_finder100k_mb, size_zip_mb = (
    f"{files['registry.csv']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}", f"{files['finder_500k.csv']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}",
    f"{files['finder_100k.csv']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}", f"{manifest['zip']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}")
md5_registry, md5_finder500k, md5_finder100k, md5_zip = (
    files["registry.csv"]["md5"], files["finder_500k.csv"]["md5"], files["finder_100k.csv"]["md5"], manifest["zip"]["md5"])

co, se, no = cfg["cohorts"], cfg["seeds"], cfg["noise"]
cfg_registry_target, cfg_finder_500k_target, cfg_finder_100k_target = n(co["registry_target"]), n(co["finder_500k_target"]), n(co["finder_100k_target"])
cfg_oversample = co["oversample"]
cfg_seed_sample, cfg_seed_registry, cfg_seed_finder, cfg_seed_postprocess = se["duckdb_sample"], se["psp_registry"], se["psp_finder"], se["postprocess"]
cfg_finder_ssn_missing, cfg_finder_ssn_transposed, cfg_finder_address_missing = pct(no["finder"]["ssn_missing"], 0), pct(no["finder"]["ssn_transposed"], 0), pct(no["finder"]["address_missing"], 0)
cfg_registry_ssn_missing, cfg_registry_ssn_transposed, cfg_registry_address_missing = pct(no["registry"]["ssn_missing"], 0), pct(no["registry"]["ssn_transposed"], 0), pct(no["registry"]["address_missing"], 0)

# deterministic ladder on the 500k finder file (results/linkage_baseline.json)
lb500  = lb["finder_files"]["finder_500k.csv"]
rules  = {r["rule"]: r for r in lb500["rules"]}
def rule(name, key):
    return round(rules[name][key], 4)
r500_name_dob_precision, r500_name_dob_recall = rule("name_dob", "precision"), rule("name_dob", "recall")
r500_name_dob_missed        = round(1 - rules["name_dob"]["recall"], 4)
r500_ssn_only_precision     = rule("ssn_only", "precision")
r500_ssn_only_missed        = round(1 - rules["ssn_only"]["recall"], 4)
r500_fcds_min_ssn_recall    = rule("fcds_min_ssn", "recall")
r500_fcds_min_monthyear_precision = rule("fcds_min_monthyear", "precision")
r500_fcds_min_monthyear_fp  = n(rules["fcds_min_monthyear"]["predicted_pairs"] - round(rules["fcds_min_monthyear"]["recall"] * lb500["true_pairs"]))
r500_fcds_either_recall, r500_fcds_either_precision = rule("fcds_min_either", "recall"), rule("fcds_min_either", "precision")
r500_fcds_current_recall    = rule("fcds_current_dob_ssn", "recall")
r500_best_recall, r500_best_precision = rule("name_dob_or_ssn", "recall"), rule("name_dob_or_ssn", "precision")
r500_best_missed            = round(1 - rules["name_dob_or_ssn"]["recall"], 4)
r500_lastname_dob_precision = rule("lastname_dob", "precision")
baseline_seconds_500k       = lb500["seconds"]

# agreement among true pairs (results/pair_agreement.json)
pa = pairs["fields"]
agree_first_name_500k, blank_first_name_500k = pct(pa["first_name"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["first_name"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_last_name_500k,  blank_last_name_500k  = pct(pa["last_name"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["last_name"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_dob_500k,        blank_dob_500k        = pct(pa["date_of_birth"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["date_of_birth"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_street_name_500k, blank_street_name_500k = pct(pa["street_name"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["street_name"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_ssn_500k,        blank_ssn_500k        = pct(pa["ssn"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["ssn"]["blank_on_either_side"])
name_dob_all_agree_500k = pct(pairs["name_dob_all_agree"])
ssn_usable_500k         = pct(pairs["ssn_usable_and_agree"])

# age/sex QA, FCDS table facts, environment
age_sex_max_dev     = round(qa["max_abs_share_deviation_pct"], 3)
by_year             = qa["rows_by_census_year"]
registry_share_2040 = pct(by_year["2040"] / sum(by_year.values()), 0)
fcds_rate_min, fcds_rate_max = round(fcds["rate"].min(), 2), round(fcds["rate"].max(), 2)
duckdb_version, psp_version, dataset_version = env["duckdb"], env["pseudopeople"], manifest["version"]
build_wall_seconds, build_peak_gb = round(env["build_wall_seconds"]), round(env["peak_rss_mb"] / 1024, 1)
run_twice = json.load(open("results/run_twice.json"))
assert run_twice["files_identical"], "the run-twice identity test failed; fix the pipeline before claiming reproducibility"
```

## Key Features {.unnumbered}

- **What is unique:** a large, fully simulated, multi-file dataset for linking individual people, with cross-file ground truth (every record carries a `simulant_id`, so missed-match and false-match rates of any method can be computed exactly rather than estimated), designed to capture the record matching challenges faced by a Florida-scale cancer data system.

- **Why created:** linkage software for cancer registries must be developed and tested on names, dates of birth, addresses and SSNs, which are exactly the identifiers that confidentiality rules prevent registries from releasing.

- **Details:** a simulated Florida drawn from the `{python} fl_pool` simulated people recorded as residents in the simulated 2020, 2030 or 2040 censuses, including a simulated registry of `{python} registry_rows` records whose age and sex distribution is that of the cases reported by the Florida Cancer Data System, and researcher finder files of `{python} finder_500k_rows` and `{python} finder_100k_rows` records drawn from residents in `{python} finder_year`.

- **Data linkage:** the larger finder file includes `{python} overlap_500k_target` people who are also in the registry and the smaller finder file includes `{python} overlap_100k_target`. There is no overlap between the finder files.

- **Main categories of data:** simulated person-level identifiers including name, date of birth, sex, street-address fields, SSN, race/ethnicity, and a diagnosis date on each registry record, carrying realistic synthetic noise (typos, nicknames, month/day swaps, blanks, duplications).

- **Access:** direct download under a permissive licence with a DOI.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Structure, contents, and where the data are held {#sec-structure}

This data resource is a zip archive containing three comma-separated files, deposited on Zenodo under a DOI that will be minted at acceptance<!-- OUTLINE run-list item 10 -->. The high-level characteristics of the files are described in @tbl-release: a simulated registry of `{python} registry_simulants` people and two finder files of `{python} finder_500k_simulants` and `{python} finder_100k_simulants` people. All three are drawn from Florida residents in the simulated 2020, 2030 or 2040 census, a pool of `{python} fl_pool` distinct simulated people. 

Every row of each file carries a `simulant_id`, the identifier of the simulated person it describes (a "simulant" in pseudopeople's vocabulary, which is what the column is named for); the same identifier in two files means the same person, and this is the ground truth against which any other linkage of the files can be scored. The files also contain the fields that record linkage typically relies on: first name, middle initial, last name, date of birth, sex, race/ethnicity, street number, street name, unit number, city, state, ZIP code and social security number (SSN). Registry rows also carry a diagnosis date, falling in one of these three years: 2020, 2030 or 2040. Addresses are for Florida cities and ZIP codes, designed to have street addresses that are not real street locations. The registry has `{python} registry_rows` rows for its `{python} registry_simulants` people, and the finder files have `{python} n(files["finder_500k.csv"]["rows"])` and `{python} n(files["finder_100k.csv"]["rows"])` rows for `{python} finder_500k_simulants` and `{python} finder_100k_simulants` people; the few people with two rows are duplicated records (@sec-methods).

The larger finder file shares `{python} overlap_500k_simulants` people with the registry, `{python} pct(match_prevalence_500k, 0)` of its records, and the smaller shares `{python} overlap_100k_simulants`, the same `{python} pct(match_prevalence_100k, 0)` share; the two finder files share no people with each other.

The archive also include a manifest of MD5 and SHA-256 digests (@tbl-release gives the MD5) and a configuration file that names every seed and design target, and the pipeline that built them is archived under its own DOI<!-- OUTLINE run-list item 10: code DOI -->. A second build from that configuration reproduced all three files byte for byte.

```{python}

    (manifest["zip"]["name"], "", "", "", size_zip_mb, md5_zip),
    ("registry.csv", registry_rows, registry_simulants, "—", size_registry_mb, md5_registry),

]
```

## Population characteristics {#sec-population}

```{python}
#| label: population-descriptives
comp = pd.read_csv("results/registry_age_sex.csv")
fold = {"Multiracial or Other": "Other", "AIAN": "Other", "NHOPI": "Other", "Unknown": "Other"}
comp["race"] = comp["race_ethnicity"].map(lambda r: fold.get(r, r if r in ("White", "Latino", "Black", "Asian") else "Other"))

def share(file, mask):
    g = comp[comp["file"] == file]
    return g[mask(g)]["count"].sum() / g["count"].sum()

def race_shares(file):
    g = comp[comp["file"] == file].groupby("race")["count"].sum()
    return (g / g.sum()).reindex(["White", "Latino", "Black", "Asian", "Other"]).fillna(0)

female_reg, female_500k = pct(share("registry.csv", lambda g: g.sex == "Female"), 0), pct(share("finder_500k.csv", lambda g: g.sex == "Female"), 0)
over65_reg, over65_500k = pct(share("registry.csv", lambda g: g.age_start >= 65), 0), pct(share("finder_500k.csv", lambda g: g.age_start >= 65), 0)
under40_reg, under40_500k = pct(share("registry.csv", lambda g: g.age_start < 40), 0), pct(share("finder_500k.csv", lambda g: g.age_start < 40), 0)
race_reg = {k: pct(v, 0) for k, v in race_shares("registry.csv").items()}
race_500k = {k: pct(v, 0) for k, v in race_shares("finder_500k.csv").items()}

# the two finder files, compared on every share quoted in this section
_shares = lambda f: pd.concat([race_shares(f), pd.Series({"female": share(f, lambda g: g.sex == "Female"),
                                                          "over65": share(f, lambda g: g.age_start >= 65),
                                                          "under40": share(f, lambda g: g.age_start < 40)})])
finder_files_max_diff_pp = f"{100 * (_shares('finder_500k.csv') - _shares('finder_100k.csv')).abs().max():.1f}"

top = pd.read_csv("results/registry_top_names.csv")
top = top[top["file"] == "registry.csv"]
def top3(sex, group):
    return ", ".join(top[(top.sex == sex) & (top.age_group == group)].sort_values("rank")["first_name"])
boys_0_4, men_85 = top3("Male", "0–4"), top3("Male", "85+")
girls_0_4, women_85 = top3("Female", "0–4"), top3("Female", "85+")
share_2020, share_2030, share_2040 = (pct(by_year[y] / sum(by_year.values()), 0) for y in ("2020", "2030", "2040"))
_n_pairs = len(pd.read_csv("results/example_pair.csv")["pair"].unique())
n_example_pairs_word = {1: "one", 2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four"}.get(_n_pairs, str(_n_pairs))
```

The simulated registry has the age and sex distribution matching the cases reported to FCDS between 1995 and 2023 [@pseudopeople_issue205]: in each of the 36 age and sex strata its share of records is within `{python} age_sex_max_dev` percentage points of FCDS's share (@fig-registry-age-sex). `{python} over65_reg` of registry records are people aged 65 or older at diagnosis and `{python} under40_reg` are under 40; `{python} female_reg` are women. The finder files have the age structure of Florida's residents in 2040 instead: `{python} over65_500k` of the larger file are 65 or older, `{python} under40_500k` are under 40, and `{python} female_500k` are female.

By race and ethnicity, people in the registry are `{python} race_reg["White"]` White, `{python} race_reg["Latino"]` Latino, `{python} race_reg["Black"]` Black, `{python} race_reg["Asian"]` Asian and `{python} race_reg["Other"]` other or multiracial, compared with `{python} race_500k["White"]`, `{python} race_500k["Latino"]`, `{python} race_500k["Black"]`, `{python} race_500k["Asian"]` and `{python} race_500k["Other"]` in the larger finder file. The two finder files differ from each other by at most `{python} finder_files_max_diff_pp` percentage points on every share reported in this section.

Registry records come from three censuses: `{python} share_2020` of them are from 2020, `{python} share_2030` from 2030 and `{python} share_2040` from 2040. Every finder record is from 2040.

The three most common first names in each age group, printed at the ends of the bars in @fig-registry-age-sex, run from `{python} boys_0_4` among boys under five to `{python} men_85` among men of 85 and over, and from `{python} girls_0_4` to `{python} women_85` among girls and women.

## Error structure {#sec-errors}

```{python}
#| label: error-structure
blank_by_file = json.load(open("results/pair_agreement.json"))["blank_share_by_file"]
pa100 = json.load(open("results/pair_agreement.json"))["finder_100k.csv"]["fields"]
FIELD_LABELS = [("first_name", "First name"), ("middle_initial", "Middle initial"), ("last_name", "Last name"),
                ("date_of_birth", "Date of birth"), ("sex", "Sex"), ("race_ethnicity", "Race/ethnicity"),
                ("street_number", "Street number"), ("street_name", "Street name"), ("unit_number", "Unit number"),
                ("city", "City"), ("state", "State"), ("zipcode", "ZIP code"), ("ssn", "SSN")]
ADDRESS = {"street_number", "street_name", "unit_number", "city", "state", "zipcode"}
def set_rate(file_kind, field):
    if field == "ssn":
        return no[file_kind]["ssn_missing"]
    if field in ADDRESS:
        return no[file_kind]["address_missing"]
    return 0.01  # pseudopeople's default leave_blank probability for every other field
def blank_cell(fname, kind, field):
    return f"{pct(blank_by_file[fname][field], 1)} ({pct(set_rate(kind, field), 0)})"
errors_100k_max_diff_pp = f"{100 * max(abs(pa[f][k] - pa100[f][k]) for f in pa for k in ('agree_when_both_present', 'blank_on_either_side')):.1f}"
unit_blank_reg = pct(blank_by_file["registry.csv"]["unit_number"], 0)
```

@tbl-errors gives the error structure field by field: the share of values that are blank in the registry and in the larger finder file, against the blanking rate set for each, and, among the `{python} overlap_500k_pairs` true pairs, the share of pairs whose two records agree exactly when both have a value and the share with a blank on either side. The smaller finder file matches the larger on every figure in the table to within `{python} errors_100k_max_diff_pp` percentage points.

SSNs are blank in `{python} finder_ssn_missing` of finder records, the rate FCDS specified, and in `{python} registry_ssn_missing` of registry records against a specified `{python} cfg_registry_ssn_missing`; the excess is structural, since `{python} pop_ssn_never` of the people in the registry pool never held an SSN in the source population. Of the SSNs present in the larger finder file, `{python} err_ssn_transposed` carry two adjacent digits swapped, and where a true pair has an SSN on both sides the two agree in `{python} agree_ssn_500k` of pairs.

Names and dates of birth disagree more often than SSNs do. Among true pairs with both values present, first names agree in `{python} agree_first_name_500k` of pairs, last names in `{python} agree_last_name_500k` and dates of birth in `{python} agree_dob_500k`, and each of these fields is blank on one side in about `{python} blank_first_name_500k` of pairs. Taken together, `{python} name_dob_all_agree_500k` of true pairs agree exactly on first name, last name and date of birth, and `{python} ssn_usable_500k` have an SSN on both sides that agrees; these two shares bound what exact-match rules can find in @sec-difficulty. Address fields agree in `{python} agree_street_name_500k` of pairs with both present and are blank on one side in `{python} blank_street_name_500k`; the unit number is blank for `{python} unit_blank_reg` of registry records, because most addresses have none, and street numbers are blank above their set rates because some source addresses carry none.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-errors
#| tbl-cap: "Error structure by field. Blank shares in the registry and the 500,000-record finder file, with the blanking rate set for each field in parentheses (FCDS's specification for SSN and address fields, pseudopeople's default elsewhere); and, among the 100,000 true pairs, the share of pairs whose two records agree exactly when both have a value and the share with a blank on either side."
#| output: asis
header = ["Field", "Blank, registry (set)", "Blank, finder file (set)", "True pairs: agree when both present", "True pairs: blank on either side"]
print("| " + " | ".join(header) + " |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|")
for f, label in FIELD_LABELS:
    print("| " + " | ".join([label, blank_cell("registry.csv", "registry", f), blank_cell("finder_500k.csv", "finder", f),
                             pct(pa[f]["agree_when_both_present"], 1), pct(pa[f]["blank_on_either_side"], 1)]) + " |")
```

## Linkage difficulty {#sec-difficulty}

```{python}
#| label: difficulty-values
fx = json.load(open("results/forensics.json"))
u = fx["uniqueness"]
uniq_name_dob, uniq_lastname_dob, uniq_zip_dob_sex = pct(u["unique_name_dob"]), pct(u["unique_lastname_dob"]), pct(u["unique_zip_dob_sex"])
shared_fullname = pct(u["share_sharing_full_name"], 0)
bl = fx["blocking"]["finder_500k.csv"]
n_pairs_naive = f"{bl['naive_pairs'] / 1e12:.1f} trillion"
pairs_block_dob = f"{bl['block_dob']['candidate_pairs'] / 1e6:.0f} million"
completeness_block_dob = pct(bl["block_dob"]["pairs_completeness"])
pairs_block_ln_yob = f"{bl['block_lastname_initial_yob']['candidate_pairs'] / 1e9:.2f} billion"
completeness_block_ln_yob = pct(bl["block_lastname_initial_yob"]["pairs_completeness"])
r500_ssn_only_recall = rule("ssn_only", "recall")
r500_current_either_recall = rule("fcds_current_either", "recall")
strat = json.load(open("results/linkage_baseline_stratified.json"))["finder_files"]["finder_500k.csv"]["rules"]
def missed(rule_name, group):
    return 1 - strat[rule_name][group]["recall"]
def fm(rule_name, group):
    return 1 - strat[rule_name][group]["precision"]
groups = ["White", "Latino", "Black", "Asian", "Other or unknown"]
nd_missed_min, nd_missed_max = pct(min(missed("name_dob", g) for g in groups)), pct(max(missed("name_dob", g) for g in groups))
nd_fm_max = pct(max(fm("name_dob", g) for g in groups), 2)
ssn_missed_white, ssn_missed_latino, ssn_missed_asian = (pct(missed("ssn_only", g), 0) for g in ("White", "Latino", "Asian"))
best_missed_white, best_missed_asian = pct(missed("name_dob_or_ssn", "White")), pct(missed("name_dob_or_ssn", "Asian"))
lb100 = lb["finder_files"]["finder_100k.csv"]
rules100 = {r["rule"]: r for r in lb100["rules"]}
ladder_100k_max_diff = f"{100 * max(abs(rules[k]['recall'] - rules100[k]['recall']) for k in rules):.1f}"
baseline_threads = lb["node"]["duckdb_threads"]
n_rules = len(rules)
```

Exact keys are less unique than they look. Among the `{python} registry_simulants` people in the registry, `{python} uniq_name_dob` have a first name, last name and date of birth that no one else in the file shares, `{python} uniq_lastname_dob` have a unique last name and date of birth, and `{python} uniq_zip_dob_sex` a unique ZIP code, date of birth and sex, while `{python} shared_fullname` share their full name with at least one other person.

@tbl-ladder scores exact-agreement rules on the larger finder file against the key. Agreement on first name, last name and date of birth links `{python} pct(r500_name_dob_recall)` of true pairs at a precision of `{python} pct(r500_name_dob_precision, 2)`, and the SSN alone links `{python} pct(r500_ssn_only_recall)` at `{python} pct(r500_ssn_only_precision, 2)`. The two field sets FCDS's Procedure Guide requires a submission to carry behave differently as exact rules: name, SSN and sex makes no false matches and finds `{python} pct(r500_fcds_min_ssn_recall)` of true pairs, name with month and year of birth and sex admits `{python} r500_fcds_min_monthyear_fp` false matches, and either set finds `{python} pct(r500_fcds_either_recall)`; the current layout's two sets, which both require the full date of birth, find `{python} pct(r500_current_either_recall)` together with no false matches. Name and date of birth or SSN, the best simple rule, reaches a recall of `{python} pct(r500_best_recall)` at a precision of `{python} pct(r500_best_precision, 2)`, and last name with date of birth alone falls to a precision of `{python} pct(r500_lastname_dob_precision)`. These are exact-agreement rules on the field sets FCDS requires a submission to carry, not the registry's own matching procedure.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ladder
#| tbl-cap: "Exact-agreement rules on the 500,000-record finder file, scored against the identity key. The Guide and layout rows are exact agreement on the field sets FCDS requires a submission to carry, not the registry's own matching procedure."
#| output: asis
SHORT = {
    "name_dob": "First name, last name, date of birth",
    "ssn_only": "SSN alone",
    "fcds_min_ssn": "Guide set: name, SSN, sex",
    "fcds_min_monthyear": "Guide set: name, month and year of birth, sex",
    "fcds_min_either": "Either Guide set",
    "fcds_current_either": "Either current layout set (name, sex, date of birth, with SSN or with address)",
    "name_dob_or_ssn": "Name and date of birth, or SSN",
    "lastname_dob": "Last name and date of birth",
}
print("| Rule | Predicted pairs | True | False | Precision | Recall | Missed-match |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
for key, label in SHORT.items():
    r = rules[key]
    print(f"| {label} | {n(r['predicted_pairs'])} | {n(r['true_positives'])} | {n(r['false_positives'])} | {r['precision']:.4f} | {r['recall']:.4f} | {pct(1 - r['recall'])} |")
```

Without blocking the two files present `{python} n_pairs_naive` record pairs. Blocking on the full date of birth leaves `{python} pairs_block_dob` candidate pairs and keeps `{python} completeness_block_dob` of true pairs; blocking on the first letter of the last name with the year of birth leaves `{python} pairs_block_ln_yob` and keeps `{python} completeness_block_ln_yob`.

@fig-stratified splits three rules by the race/ethnicity recorded on the finder record. For first name, last name and date of birth the missed-match rate is alike across groups, from `{python} nd_missed_min` to `{python} nd_missed_max`, and the false-match rate stays below `{python} nd_fm_max` in every group. The SSN rule differs by group: it misses `{python} ssn_missed_asian` of true pairs for Asian people and `{python} ssn_missed_latino` for Latino people against `{python} ssn_missed_white` for White people, and the difference carries into the best simple rule, which misses `{python} best_missed_asian` of Asian true pairs against `{python} best_missed_white` of White ones.

```{python}
#| label: fig-stratified
#| fig-cap: "Missed-match and false-match rates of three exact-agreement rules on the 500,000-record finder file, by the race/ethnicity recorded on the finder record, with the number of true pairs in each group."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.09, 3.1), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.3, 1]})
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.27, right=0.99, top=0.97, bottom=0.27, wspace=0.08)
handles = F.stratified_baseline(ax1, ax2)
fig.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower center", ncol=3, frameon=False, fontsize=7, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.0))
plt.show()
```

The `{python} n_rules` rules run in `{python} baseline_seconds_500k` seconds on the 500,000-record file with `{python} baseline_threads` threads on an eight-core allocation. The 100,000-record file gives the same picture: every rule's recall is within `{python} ladder_100k_max_diff` percentage points of the larger file's.
